subject: SLA dimensioning & hardware choice — post-call recs
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: James Ellis <j.ellis@medsolve.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jan 2028 15:23:00 +0000
Subject: SLA dimensioning & hardware choice — post-call recs

Hi James — great to meet today. Quick recap from our side and concrete next steps so we stay aligned on MedSolve's latency/throughput requirements for the pilot.

Call highlights:
- Target p95 latency: 120ms for single-request chat (streaming enabled)
- Expected steady-state qps: 220 requests/sec with bursts to 500 QPS for 1–2 min windows
- Average tokens per request: 160 (prompt + expected response)
- Concurrency model: up to 60 concurrent streaming sessions during peak
- Critical: KV prefix caching and short-circuiting must be enabled for repeat prompts

Our ask from MedSolve this week:
1) Confirm whether 120ms p95 is strict or a soft target for the pilot
2) Share any non-functional constraints (fixed-region hosting, data residency)
3) If possible, provide a small representative prompt set we can use for the throughput bench

Preliminary recommendations (internal note included in the attachment):
- Reserved capacity candidate: 2x A100-style 80GB-equivalent GPUs vs 4x A10/A30-class SKUs depending on concurrency shapes
- For streaming-heavy workloads, prefer fewer high-memory cards (larger KV cache) to reduce cross-GPU hops
- Use quantized 4-bit configs only after quality checks; initial pilot should be FP16/AMP for stability

Attachments: gpu_matrix_v2.pdf (hardware comparison), throughput-latency-sim.csv (pilot sim inputs)

Next steps:
- James: confirm p95 flexibility and share the prompt set by Tue 17 Jan
- Karthik & Mina: run a short bench (2–4h) on both SKU families once we have the prompt set; we'll share results and a recommended reserved throughput number

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Priya — helpful recap. Two quick clarifications: we can be flex on p95 in week 0 (goalable to 150ms) but for production after pilot we need to be at or under 120ms. Data residency: US-only region ok.

I'll paste a representative prompt set (5 prompts) below and drop the full dataset to your Drive link by Monday. The attached examples include long-context prompts that may increase token averages.

Representative prompts:
1) "Retrieve patient summary and list outstanding labs." (~90 tokens)
2) "Summarize last 6 months of discharge notes and call out medication changes." (~340 tokens)
3) "Prioritize follow-ups for high-risk patients with diabetes." (~150 tokens)
4) "Generate patient-facing explanation of diagnosis in lay terms." (~70 tokens)
5) "Compose a templated referral letter including sections A, B, and C." (~220 tokens)

We can be available for the bench run window Tue afternoon. One ask: can you show us results for both (a) 2x80GB-class GPUs and (b) 4xA30-class as a side-by-side throughput/latency table? That will help procurement.

- James
James Ellis
VP Product, MedSolve Health

Priya / Mina — copying our internal bench plan here so we can move quickly once James uploads the prompt set. I'm planning a two-pass bench:

Pass 1 (functional):
- Run 30-minute sample on both SKU families with the five representative prompts (single-run concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 24, 48, 64)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU mem utilization, KV cache hit rate
- Mode: FP16, streaming enabled, batch size tuned for latency (no quantized runs yet)

Pass 2 (stress and reserved throughput estimation):
- Run 2-hour steady-state run at target QPS (220) and configured bursts to 500 QPS for 2 minutes every 15 minutes
- Measure tail latencies and backpressure behavior; estimate headroom and recommended reserved throughput (requests/sec equivalent)

Pre-bench configuration notes (to avoid re-runs):
- Use prefix caching with a 30-minute TTL, warm KV cache with the representative prompt set
- Ensure model variants are pinned identically across SKUs (same weights/quantization)
- Collect per-request trace IDs and token-level timing for post-run analysis

I'll prepare a short summary template that maps bench outputs to a recommended reserved capacity (e.g., "2x80GB -> reserved throughput 360 rps; 4xA30 -> reserved throughput 240 rps, with expected p95 140ms"). That template will be filled after the runs.

Mina — can you confirm access to a region-hosted A100-equivalent bench for Tue 18:00 UTC? If not, we'll shift to Wed.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer
[Internal note: ensure we capture streaming stall metrics]

All set — I reserved the bench pool for Tue 18:00 UTC: 2x80GB equiv (label: bench-a100-2x) and 4xA30 equiv (label: bench-a30-4x). I've attached a short runbook with toggles we'll use (warm cache, streaming flags, batch knobs).

Runbook highlights:
- Warm step: replay 1000 typical requests to populate KV cache before steady-state
- Telemetry: token timestamps + GPU-side kernel timelines (for cross-GPU hops)
- Fallback policy: if tail p95 > 300ms during burst, we'll enable additional batching to observe tradeoffs, then revert

I'll upload logs and a filled recommendation matrix to the Drive link within 6 hours of completion.
